messages:
alex: Heads-up — we've been hitting repeated GPU capacity shortfalls in eu-west spot pools during nightly batching windows. Thinking we should add a warmup buffer + deferred scaling behavior to the autoscaler Helm values so spot nodes are provisioned earlier and not immediately torn down. Anyone seen similar flapping?

jmiller: yep, noticed pods Pending with no nodes around 02:15-02:40 for 3 nights. Logs show cluster-autoscaler kept cycling scale up/down.

sara: can you paste the CA logs for one incident? I want to confirm it was scale-down reclaiming nodes that still had pods in NotReady state.

alex: here — trimmed: ```I0323 02:16:12.345678 1 scale_up.go:200] No template: node template for gpu-spot-eu-west ; trigger scale-up for 6 cores``````I0323 02:17:02.987654 1 scale_down.go:145] Removing node gpu-spot-xyz — empty, but had pods in Terminating >10m```

jmiller: that Terminating >10m is the killer — evicting GPUs takes longer (nvidia-drivers + kubelet drain). CA thinks node is empty but kubelet not finished -> race.

tina: two quick ideas: 1) add a warm_pool min size (1-2 nodes) in terraform for node groups so we have instant capacity, 2) tweak autoscaler Helm: set scaleDownDelayAfterAdd: 30m and set unneededTime to 15m for gpu pools.

sara: +1 on changing CA timing. Also suggest "deferredScaleMode" pattern — we keep a lightweight cached capacity (warm nodes) and only let CA aggressively scale down if metrics show >30m of idle.

alex: drafting a helm values snippet now — want feedback: ```autoscaler:
  enabled: true
  extraArgs:
    scale-down-delay-after-add: "30m"
    unneeded-time: "15m"
    gpu-node-pool: "true"
  warmup:
    enabled: true
    minWarmNodes: 1
    preemptibleWarm: true
```

jmiller: OK. For terraform node group we can expose warm_pool_count and preemptible flag. Example: ```resource "eks_node_group" "gpu_spot" {
  instance_types = ["p4d.24xlarge"]
  desired_size = 0
  max_size = 50
  tags = { role = "gpu-spot" }
  warm_pool = { size = 1, mode = "Stop" }
}
```

tina: careful — warm_pool Stop/Start semantics differ across clouds. For our managed clusters warm_pool Stop creates quicker launch but still counts toward quotas. Need to validate IP/ENI quotas in eu-west2.

sara: cost tradeoff: 1 warm node ~ $X/day but prevents ~30m cold-start tail latency for many requests. For nightly batch this looks worth it. Also recommend adding `taint: gpu-warm:NoSchedule` so only batch-controller can use warm nodes until fully ready.

alex: good call on taints. We should also add an autoscaler rollout with canary: enable warmup in dev cluster first, watch node churn and Pending pod latency, then prod.

jmiller: infra-bot just reported a recent scale event during window: ```infra-bot: [02:23] autoscaler scaled up 4 nodes in gpu-spot-eu-west (reason: unschedulable pods)``````infra-bot: [02:31] autoscaler scaled down 5 nodes in gpu-spot-eu-west (reason: empty nodes)```

tina: exact race. To avoid the CA mis-detecting emptiness we can hook into kubelet drain grace: extend terminationGracePeriodSeconds for GPU daemons, or annotate pods so CA waits. But extending TGPS is scary for latency on scale-down.

sara: alternative: pre-drain eviction webhook that marks nodes as "protect-warm" for 20m so CA ignores them. Might be heavy to implement.

alex: plan proposal: 1) terraform change to add warm_pool_count variable (1 default) to gpu spot node groups; 2) helm values change to set scaleDownDelayAfterAdd=30m and unneededTime=15m for gpu pools and add warmup flags; 3) deploy canary to dev eu-west, monitor for 48h; 4) if stable roll to prod.

jmiller: SGTM. I'll open a PR for terraform module + docs. Will add a smoke test: run 30 concurrent batch pods and measure time-to-scheduled.

tina: I'll adjust quotas/ENI checks for eu-west and run a dry-run on a staging cluster. Heads-up: if warm_pool counts toward reserved capacity, billing team needs to approve for prod.

sara: add metrics we should track during canary: node churn rate, avg pod pending time, number of terminating pods >5m, autoscaler scale-up/scale-down events.

alex: thanks — I'll draft the PR and the canary runbook. tagging @tina @jmiller for follow-up. :thumbsup:
